findings.problem: The content frames the warehouse as having expensive storage per unit ('저장 비쌈'), and the storage meter backs this up with a warehouse segment longer than the lake segment. That is out of date and nothing discloses the simplification. Managed storage in today's cloud warehouses costs about the same per TB as object storage. The real cost of keeping two copies is double storage plus duplicate loading and compute, sync jobs, and proprietary formats. Minjae's line in the solution scene repeats the same framing.

findings.problem: The note on the 1-hour step says running the batch more often leaves the load 'almost unchanged'. That contradicts the step's own bars, which double cost (1→2) and ops (1→2). It is also wrong in practice: if every run recomputes everything, compute cost grows with the number of runs, which is 24 times a day here. Only the orchestration effort stays roughly the same.

findings.problem: The ML training data reads review text straight from Bronze, the raw layer, while the text promises that customer info leaves only as pseudonymized columns. Raw review rows usually carry the reviewer's customer ID, and the free text can include names or phone numbers. Reading Bronze directly skips both the Silver cleanup taught in Ch8 and the Ch9 privacy controls. As written, the 'pseudonymized columns only' promise is not guaranteed, and nothing in the scene mentions it.

findings.problem: The text says any date condition triggers pruning. Pruning only happens when the filter is on the partition column, here the order date, and is written in a form the engine can prune on. A filter on another date column, such as 배송일, still scans every partition.

findings.problem: The catalog lists the customer-center team as owner of the customer table, yet in the same chapter that team sees only masked values. The data owner is usually the producing domain (member service) or the data team, which is accountable for the data and approves access. A consuming team that can't see the full values is an odd owner and blurs the governance lesson.

Worst-case freshness is really the run interval plus processing time: a 15-minute schedule with a 3-minute job can be 18 minutes stale. That would fail the '15분 이내' criterion the scale marks as met. The model is labeled simplified, but this particular gap is not mentioned.

Sora works only with pseudonymized keys (Ch9), so the scene reads as if pseudonymized data is being re-identified. Nothing mentions consent or that an authorized pipeline does the linking.

content2.summary: I audited the content for ch4, ch5, ch6 and ch7: every step text, dialogue line, figure label, alt text, interaction string and quiz in src/content/chapters/ch4–ch7.ts. I also read the matching A–Z cards in src/content/cards.ts and the '정확성 메모' notes in docs/storyboard/05–08. I checked all the arithmetic and none of it is wrong: Ch4's 119,000/72,000 order sums, the 30/30 vs 12/30 cell counts and the dictionary codes; every row and delta in Ch5's worker-slider model (960/n + (n−1) + 20); Ch6's job timings and the ~19h gap; Ch7's daily figures and the SUM(NULL)-shown-as-0 logic. Invented real-world statistics: none. Every number is labelled 가상 or belongs to the fictional company. Nothing is outright factually wrong (no high severity). There are 7 medium findings. Six are content issues: (1) Ch4's '총매출' includes cancelled and refunded orders, unlike the real accounting term, and the on-screen disclaimer is only generic; (2) Ch4 says '분석용 DB' is row-oriented and bad at big aggregations, which reads as a general rule; (3) Ch4 star-schema step 4 gives 욕실 40,000 / 주방 16,000, but the three fact rows on screen add up to 24,000 / 8,000; (4) Ch5 implies 'file bigger than RAM → you need distributed processing' and never mentions reading in chunks on one machine; (5) Ch6 says the detector '결제를 보류' (holds the payment), but it reads payments that have already completed; (6) Ch6's subway example presents a payment event as created on the phone. The seventh is the lead's Ch4 dot-overlap issue, which is real (details below). There are 14 low findings covering term precision and clarity: dbt vs version control, the shuffle's partial aggregation, the slider's cost note, micro-batch nuance in the summary, Kafka consumer-group wording, the processing-time definition, tumbling windows vs the '5분 안에' rule, the broker's 'in order' definition, the timing of the 18:05 test, the idempotent rerun, the gate metaphor, YAML vs the test tool, the Ch4 back-reference, and the breaking-rename practice. One low finding is on card Q. The lead's Ch4 issue: on mobile, the accent particles (circle[data-el="sp2"]) sit over '주문 항목 팩트' and '1~3일치만 담은 예시' partway through step 4 (screenshot /Users/kimtaewoo/DE_web/shots/acc47/starm-01-m.png). At desktop near step end (@0.95) the dots have faded. I did not check the other known issues (Epilogue, Ch1, Ch2) because they are outside ch4–7. Screenshots are in /Users/kimtaewoo/DE_web/shots/acc47/.

findings.problem: "총매출 … 주문된 금액 그대로의 합계 · 할인 전 · 배송비 포함 · 취소·환불 포함" (figures.defs[0], solution step 1 alt, scene 2 soraRules). In real accounting, 총매출 normally leaves out cancelled orders. A total that includes cancelled and refunded orders plus shipping is usually called 거래액(GMV) or 주문 금액. The only disclaimer is the generic "실제 회계 기준은 더 복잡하지만, 여기서는 바구니가 정한 정의예요." A beginner will leave thinking 총매출 includes cancellations. The storyboard (05-ch4 정확성 메모) admits this but nothing on screen says it.
findings.evidence: ch4.ts figures.defs[0].rules = '할인 전 · 배송비 포함 · 취소·환불 포함'; figures.accountingNote; storyboard 05-ch4.md 정확성 메모: "실제 회계의 총매출은 보통 취소된 주문을 넣지 않고…"
findings.fix: Make accountingNote specific: "실제 회계의 총매출은 보통 취소된 주문을 빼요. 여기서는 바구니가 내부에서 정한 정의예요." (Alternative: rename the metric to '주문 금액(거래액)' wherever '총매출' appears.)

findings.problem: Attempt step 3 says "분석용 DB는 한 건씩 다루기 좋은 구조라, 큰 집계에 약했거든요." Warehouse step 3 says "분석용 DB는 운영 DB와 같은 행 기반 저장(…)을 써요." Both read as general facts: a database named 'for analytics' that is built for single rows and is bad at analytics. That contradicts itself for a beginner. It is really a story assumption: Ch2 loaded into the same kind of DB engine as the operational DB. Ch2's code runner even accepts 'warehouse' as an alias for 분석용 DB (ch2.ts targets).

content1.summary: Content accuracy audit of prologue, ch1, ch2 and ch3. I read src/content/chapters/{prologue,ch1,ch2,ch3}.ts in full, plus the backing strings in src/content/map.ts and src/content/cards.ts. Nothing is factually wrong enough to rate high. Every acronym expansion is correct (CSV, JSON, SQL, OLTP/OLAP, ETL/ELT, DAG), and so are the definitions (idempotency, backfill, retry, schema, structured/semi-structured/unstructured data). The cards S, U, J, O, E, B, A, D and I are fine. The in-story arithmetic all checks out: 1,532 − 5 = 1,527; 9 items with P1 = 4; raw revenue 10,000 vs real 19,000 won; the 3/2/1 date split; 1,800/1,200 = 1.5×. No invented real-world statistics: all numbers are in-story, and the exaggerated DB-load gauge is already disclosed (ch1 loadNote). The Ch1 SQL runner's aggregate behaviour matches real SQL: SUM over no rows gives NULL, COUNT gives 0, GROUP BY over no rows returns no rows (sql.ts:477). Four medium findings: (1) a Prologue note that teaches a wrong rule for what gets stored ("장바구니는 돈이 안 오가서 이벤트 로그에만"); (2) after Ch1 shows the CSV is an export of 운영 DB, the map still draws it as coming from the app (map.ts:130); (3) the Ch2 운영 DB holds '4,000원' and three date formats, which contradicts the typed schema taught in the Prologue, with no disclosure; (4) the Ch3 DAG has no load step, yet the text sets "적재: 그날 치 덮어쓰기". The rest are low-severity clarity or senior-practice notes (backfill needs a date parameter, alert policy is inconsistent, ETL vs batch blurred, PII missing as a reason to choose ETL, value case sensitivity in the SQL runner help, and others). Of the lead's known issues, I verified the two in my chapters on a 390×844 mobile viewport. Both are real. The Ch2 runner has a 185px empty band in the finished state in BOTH ETL and ELT (not only ELT). The Ch1 runner leaves 127px empty at step 1 (FROM); the gap shrinks to 7px by the last step. The Ch4 star-schema and Epilogue tag issues are outside prologue–ch3 and I did not verify them. findings.problem: interaction.notes.cart (L41) says "장바구니는 아직 돈이 오가지 않아서 이벤트 로그에만 남아요." The causal rule is wrong. Whether something is stored in the service DB depends on whether the service needs to remember it, not on whether money moves. In a real shop the cart contents are persisted in the operational DB (or a session store) so the cart survives a page reload. Ch1 then shows the ops DB holding products and customers tables, which aren't money either, so learners hit a contradiction. The real distinction is: the add_to_cart *action* goes to the event log, the cart *state* is stored by the service, and neither is a confirmed transaction.

keyboard.summary:
I tested keyboard and screen-reader use at 1440x900 and 390x844 (mobile), in normal and reduced-motion modes, against http://localhost:5288/?mount=all. A full Tab pass from the top reaches 157 stops on desktop and 160 on mobile, and wraps back to the skip link with no keyboard trap. Focus order is logical: skip link, motion toggle, HUD button, 12 rail links, hero, then each chapter's interaction, quiz and growth replay, then the epilogue map, dex, links and restart.

What works: almost every focused element shows a visible 3px accent ring, including on the dark blueprint chapters. In the HUD dialog, the tabs work with Left/Right arrows, Esc closes it and focus goes back to the opener. TOC links and map nodes close the dialog and move focus to the chapter h2. Quiz radios work with arrow keys, and Enter submits. The ranges have aria-valuetext. Ch3 keeps focus on the retry button by using aria-disabled, and Ch8 moves focus to the slider when it disables a button. The epilogue restart dialog focuses 취소 and Esc returns focus. There are no unnamed buttons, no broken ARIA id references, no duplicate ids and no focusable elements inside aria-hidden. All 102 role=img elements (289 in reduced mode) have labels, and plain scrolling fires no live-region announcements. The heading outline is one h1, an h2 per chapter and an h3 per scene.

The most serious problem: the skip link is invisible when focused (1x1px, clipped). The root cause is that the unlayered global .sr-only and :focus-visible rules in src/styles/index.css beat Tailwind's layered utilities. The same cause hides the selected state of the motion-preference options and produces double focus rings in the Ch2 editor and on the epilogue map nodes. Other confirmed problems: focus is lost to the page body after a quiz is submitted and after the HUD reset confirm or cancel; the growth card rows become unnamed tab stops when they overflow; card tiles carry their text only in aria-label while the visible text is aria-hidden; the quiz, summary and growth blocks have no headings; there are 106 region landmarks; and turning on 모션 줄이기 moves the reader about two scenes back.

The lead's known issues, checked: Ch1 SQL runner on mobile is real (svg 351px tall, only 118px visible after the JOIN query runs, so 233px is empty). Ch2 ELT on mobile is real (about 200px empty belt band). The epilogue zoom step 4 issue is partly real: tags and the Ch8 callout overlap node borders and edges, but not the label text. The Ch4 star-schema step 4 dot overlap did not reproduce in frames sampled at 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 of step 4; the dots only move along the arrows, so it may only happen briefly in between. A flaky case where Tab sometimes stopped on two radios in one quiz group (seen once in Ch3, Ch6, Ch7 and Ch9) did not reproduce consistently, so I left it out. Scripts and screenshots are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kimtaewoo-DE-web/87f927fd-5f5a-4ca9-8840-608bdfafed08/scratchpad/a11y/ and /Users/kimtaewoo/DE_web/shots/a11y/.

findings.problem: The skip link '본문으로 건너뛰기' stays invisible when focused. The unlayered .sr-only rule (index.css:113) beats Tailwind's layered focus:not-sr-only / focus:fixed utilities on the link in App.tsx:16, so it never expands.

contrast.summary:
I audited color and contrast across all 12 stage palettes and found 1 high, 12 medium and 9 low findings.

**How it was checked**
- `node scripts/contrast.mjs` passes on every stage (exit 0).
- I wrote a Playwright scanner that does three things on desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844:
  - It scrolls each scrub step to its end state (t ≈ i+0.93) and sweeps the whole page at 0.6-viewport intervals.
  - For every visible HTML or SVG text it takes the fill/color and the product of ancestor opacity, and reads the background as the pixel mode around the text in a screenshot.
  - It records the rendered font size in pixels.
- A second pass ran every interaction (Prologue shop, Ch1 SQL examples, Ch2 code examples, Ch3 DAG fail and retry, Ch5/Ch8/Ch10 sliders, Ch10 toggles), answered every quiz, and replayed every growth sequence.
- A third pass scanned SVG strokes at each step end.

**What passes**
- Every colored word drawn in fail/ok (실패, 시간 초과, 품절, 실제와 달라요, ✕ 미달, ✓ 충족, …) passes 4.5:1 where it actually sits. The one borderline case is Ch6 at 4.49.
- The accent color is only ever used for glyphs (↻ ▶). The lowest is 3.30 on the stage-7 card color, which still passes the 3:1 rule for non-text.
- Proposal and dashed elements pass: dashed lines at 0.78 opacity reach 5.6–7.5:1, and the muted '제안' label reaches 4.8:1 in stage 10.
- I found no status shown by color alone. Badges, DagSimulator, Quiz, TimeTravel and TradeoffScale all pair a glyph with text. The Ch4 star step-4 join lines also differ in width (3.4 vs ~1.55).
- Disabled controls at opacity 0.55 are exempt. That covers 정답 확인, 이전/다음 버전 and the DAG 재시도 button with `aria-disabled`.

**Real problems**
1. **NEW tag on blueprint stages (high):** the '새로' tag is white text on the accent color, which gives 2.35:1 in Ch7–Ch10 growth maps. It renders at 5.6px on desktop and 3.6–4px on mobile.
2. **Chapter rail over the Ch6→Ch7 band:** the rail's numbers use stage-6 ink but sit over the dark gradient band, giving 2.23–4.45:1.
3. **Deliberately dimmed text you still need to read** falls to 1.9–4.0:1:
   - Ch1 excluded rows: 1.86
   - Ch4 discount/shipping values: 2.46–2.57
   - Ch4 warehouse cells: 1.86–2.37
   - Ch9 original PII table: 3.99
   - Ch10 plan board: 2.33
   - Ch10 recall label: 3.61
   - Ch5 partition paths: 2.59
   - Ch8 sync: 1.88
   - background-ghost layers in Prologue, Ch2, Ch6, Ch7, Ch10 and the Epilogue: as low as 1.37
4. **Muted text on tinted fills:** Ch3 '지난밤' is 3.99:1 and Ch6 '품절인데' is 4.49:1.
5. **HUD progress bar:** the accent fill against its track is 1.80–3.02:1, failing 3:1 in stages 2–11.
6. **Very small text in growth and thumbnail maps:** labels render at 5–8px on desktop and 3.6–5.4px on mobile.
7. **`contrast.mjs` blind spots:** it checks fail/ok only at 3:1 even though they are used for words. It never checks white-on-accent, wait-on-card, or muted text at 0.78 opacity.
8. **Text selection** is white on accent, which is also 2.35:1 on blueprint stages.

**Lead's known issues — all four are real**
- **Ch4 star step 4:** the dot overlap is transient. At step position ~0.75–0.80 the `sp2` particles sit on top of '주문 항목 팩트' and on the '3' of '1~3일치만 담은 예시'. They are gone by the end of the step.
- **Epilogue zoom step 4:** the chapter tags overlap node tops. The Ch8 tag covers the 레이크하우스 cylinder top, and the Ch5 and Ch3 tags are clipped at the right edge.
- **Ch1 SQL runner on mobile:** after a run finishes, the empty space under the result is 96–233px. Examples 4 and 5 leave a 351px-tall SVG with content ending at 118px.
- **Ch2 code runner on mobile, ELT example:** there is about a 190px empty band between the belt and the 분석용 DB.

**Lighthouse 12.8.2 accessibility**
- Five runs: desktop, mobile, desktop scrolled to `#ch7`, `#ch10` and `#epilogue`. All scored 0.93, and the color-contrast audit passed every time. That audit does not check SVG `<text>` or opacity states, so it misses everything above.
- Three audits failed:
  - `aria-prohibited-attr`: 48 items, all from `<g data-check aria-label="품질 검사">` in `PipelineMap.tsx:105`.
  - `label-content-name-mismatch`: 48 items, covering the HUD button, the 5 DAG nodes, 19 map links and 26 dex buttons.
  - `definition-list`: 1 item, at `Ch10/scenes.tsx:747`.

**Files**
All scratch files are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kimtaewoo-DE-web/87f927fd-5f5a-4ca9-8840-608bdfafed08/scratchpad/color/`:
- scripts: `scan.mjs`, `interact.mjs`, `lib.mjs`, `strokes.mjs`, `stepshot.mjs`, `runners.mjs`, `agg.mjs`, `tok.mjs`, `combos.mjs`
- results: `out/scan-d.json`, `out/scan-m.json`, `out/interact-d.json`, `out/interact-m.json`, `out/strokes-d.txt`
- screenshots: `out/shots/`, `out/ishots/`, `known/`
- Lighthouse reports: `lh/*.json`

**False positives I ruled out**
- Ch1 '■ 중지': two overlapping elements cross-fade.
- Ch2 'data =': text inside a closed `<details>`.
- Ch1 transparent mirror text in the SQL editor.
- Mobile step text that had scrolled underneath the sticky diagram.
- Mid-transition frames, such as the Epilogue dex 'Ch6' row at 0.53 opacity.

mobile.summary:
I audited mobile layout at 390×844 and 360×740 (isMobile, DPR 2, ?mount=all). I measured the end state of all 209 scene steps in the DOM: rendered SVG text size, text overlap, clipping, step text height against the strip left visible below the sticky diagram, and horizontal overflow. I took screenshots of the first and last step of every scene, every opening, every interaction (I operated each one: ran SqlRunner/CodeRunner with every experiment, moved sliders to both ends, clicked nodes and buttons), every quiz (answer submitted) and every growth block, plus the epilogue MapNav, DexBoard and Restart blocks. There was no horizontal page scroll in any state (scrollWidth == innerWidth at both widths) and there were 0 console errors.

All four issues the lead flagged are real. (1) Ch4 star step 4: the sp2 particles cross '주문 항목 팩트' and '1~3일치만 담은 예시' while they travel (f 0.75–0.85). (2) Epilogue zoom step 4: the chapter tags sit on node outlines (Ch8 over the lakehouse rim and highlight ring), and the right column is clipped by about 3px at 390. No tag covers label text. (3) Ch1 SqlRunner: the stage keeps the height of its tallest phase, leaving about 220px blank under a 4-row result. (4) Ch2 CodeRunner: a fixed band of about 200px sits empty for the whole ELT run, and also after an ETL run.

The biggest problem is text size across the whole page. 54% of visible diagram text renders below 11px at 390, and 70% at 360. The cause is the 440-wide viewBox drawn into a 358px or 328px box. Pipeline-map overviews are unreadable: in the growth blocks from Ch5 on they render at 3.6–5.6px, and they are just as small inside scenes. Two layout problems appear only at 360×740: the Ch10 ADR card spills out of the sticky panel, and 13 step text blocks are taller than the 296–326px strip below the sticky diagram. Touch targets: `.btn-sm` is 36px (HUD, replay buttons, experiment buttons), and the Ch5 row toggles are 33×20. Screenshots are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kimtaewoo-DE-web/87f927fd-5f5a-4ca9-8840-608bdfafed08/scratchpad/mob/ (s390, s360, t390, t360, i390, i360, run390, crop), and the raw measurements are in steps-m390.json and steps-m360.json.

I checked SPEC 10 end to end with playwright on ?mount=all, starting from empty localStorage: desktop 1440, mobile 390 and 375, and reduced motion. Two things fail, both from one shared bug.

**What fails**
1. **Lv5 is never reached on ?mount=all (high).** Answering a quiz, a growth section expanding and running the SQL runner all make the page taller, but nothing recalculates the ScrollTrigger positions. Every scroll trigger below then fires too early: by +352px after the prologue quiz and +1150px after three quizzes. The normal lazy-loading flow does reach Lv5 26/26, because later chapter mounts happen to refresh. Going back to answer an earlier quiz after everything is mounted still leaves 56 triggers stale by 352px. The fix belongs in one place: a ResizeObserver next to the ScrollTrigger setup in src/lib/gsap.ts.
2. **Ch10 climax can be earned by skipping (low).** Jumping past Ch10 via the rail or a link grants it, so a reader with nothing done sees 'Lv2 주니어 0/26'. In reduced motion the same jump stays at Lv1.

SCROLL TEST: steady 1500 px/s, frame gaps from requestAnimationFrame, long tasks from PerformanceObserver plus long-animation-frame attribution, all with ?mount=all.
- Dev server, 1x CPU: 25 frames over 50ms, one at every chapter boundary (67-113ms, from the ChapterShell IntersectionObserver re-render in dev React), plus prologue-attempt 267ms and epilogue-zoom 233ms.
- Production build, 1x CPU: only 6 frames over 50ms (ch3-solution 50, ch6-solution 67, epilogue-dex 83 and 100).

- Production, 4x CPU, mobile 390px: 67 frames over 50ms and 72 long tasks totalling 7.1s.

Root cause of the scroll jank: SVG text is re-laid out at every new scale. Whenever a viewBox camera tween, mapTransition or scale tween changes an SVG's scale, Chromium re-shapes every `<text>` at the new pixel size, costing about 2-3ms per text and 50-60ms per frame for the ch3/ch4/ch6/ch8 diagrams. Containment does not help (tested). Adding `text-rendering: geometricPrecision` to SVG text drops it to 0.1-0.2ms. With that one CSS rule:
- 4x desktop: 3 frames over 50ms, 2 long tasks totalling 118ms.
- 4x mobile: 5 frames over 50ms, 2 long tasks totalling 215ms.
- A 1x-DPR screenshot of the ch6 diagram text looks identical with and without it.

REAL-USER LAZY MOUNT: with the text fix, the remaining jank is chapter mounting. At 1x, 15 long tasks totalled 1.3s. findings.problem: Scrubbed camera moves (attr viewBox tweens in Ch03/Ch05/Ch06/Ch07/Ch08 and PipelineMap mapTransition) and scale tweens (Epilogue dex tiles) force Chromium to re-shape every SVG <text> at each new device scale. That costs 50-66ms per frame on an unthrottled M-series machine and 100-450ms per frame at 4x CPU. This is the dominant source of scroll jank.
findings.evidence: Changing the scale on the ch6-solution SVG (48 texts) costs 57-61ms per frame, ch4-solution 50-52ms, ch3-solution 50-52ms, ch8-problem 50ms. Hiding all text makes it 0ms. Per text it is about 1.7-3.3ms; Badge glyph texts (⏸ 10.35px/700, ✕ 9.2px/700) cost about 16ms each. With `text-rendering: geometricPrecision` the cost is 0.1-0.2ms. `contain:strict` on the diagram box did not help (4x run still had 47 frames over 50ms). Full scroll at 4x desktop: 39 frames over 50ms and 40 long tasks (4.58s) become 3 frames and 2 long tasks (118ms). At 4x mobile: 67 frames and 72 long tasks (7.1s) become 5 frames and 2 long tasks (215ms). Worst scenes before the fix: epilogue-dex 450ms, ch6-solution 300, ch3-solution 217, ch8-problem 200, ch4-solution 167, ch5-attempt 167, epilogue-zoom/cycle 100. A 1x-DPR screenshot of the ch6 diagram text looks the same before and after (scratchpad/perf/vis-ch6-*.png).
findings.fix: Add one global rule to index.css: `svg text { text-rendering: geometricPrecision; }`. This lays SVG text out once and scales it geometrically, so viewBox/scale tweens stop re-shaping text. No change to build functions is needed. Re-check small labels on a 1x monitor.

findings.problem: Lighthouse mobile Performance is 78 (77-82 across runs), below the SPEC 90 target. The 99 @font-face rules (52 KB of the 99.7 KB render-blocking CSS) make Chromium request 11 Pretendard subsets plus JetBrains Mono (about 360 KB) at VeryHigh priority before first paint. Lantern then counts them on the FCP/LCP critical path.
findings.evidence: Mobile: FCP 3.6s, LCP 4.2s, SI 3.6s; LCP element is the hero `p.mt-6` with 89% render delay. Observed FCP is 49ms. network-requests shows 12 VeryHigh woff2 files requested at 38ms. Experiment in scratchpad/perf/dist-exp: I moved the @font-face blocks into assets/fonts.css and injected that link on `load`+rAF. In main.tsx: `addEventListener('load', () => import('./styles/fonts.css').then(() => document.fonts.ready).then(refreshTriggers), { once: true })`. Keep the existing fallback stacks so text renders immediately. Re-running refreshTriggers after the swap matters because the current `document.fonts.ready` call in main.tsx will resolve before these fonts are requested.

findings.problem: In real (lazy-mount) browsing every chapter mount happens during a scroll gesture. It produces a synchronous React Suspense commit, during which the useGSAP builds force style and layout of the whole new chapter, followed by a forced layout in a ScrollTrigger scroll handler. The very first scroll stalls while the Prologue mounts.
findings.evidence: Production lazy run at 1x (with the text fix): 13 frames over 50ms, 15 long tasks (1.29s), all at chapter entry. Each mount is a `TimerHandler:setTimeout` task in index.js (React reveal) of 48-159ms, with 41-137ms of forced layout, plus `#document.onscroll` gsap tasks of 55-76ms forced. Examples: first scroll 'top' 169ms, prologue 123, ch2 136, ch9 167. At 4x: 25 long tasks (4.7s) of 165-564ms each.
findings.fix: Mount ahead of need during idle time instead of on the scroll that reaches the 150% rootMargin. When chapter k becomes active (setActive in Chapter.tsx), call `requestIdleCallback(() => startTransition(() => ensureMounted(k + 1)), { timeout: 3000 })` (fall back to setTimeout). Do the same after `load` for index 0 instead of waiting for the first scroll. Keep the IntersectionObserver as a fallback. If that is not enough, defer each StepScene's useGSAP build until its section is within about one viewport (an IntersectionObserver in ScrubScene), which spreads the forced layout across scenes.

findings.problem: Any progress change (reach() on each newly reached chapter, markClimax() at ch10-decision) re-renders every useProgress consumer. That includes whole-chapter roots: Ch10() uses useProgress only for markClimax, and Ch07/Epilogue blocks also subscribe. The result is a long task at chapter boundaries and at the climax.
findings.evidence: Dev server 1x: an IntersectionObserver callback in Chapter.tsx takes 83-113ms at every chapter start (ch1@0.00, ch2@0.00 ... epilogue@0.00). Production 4x: IO callbacks 36-51ms. ch10-decision 'MessagePort.onmessage' React task 69-96ms at 4x (54ms in the lazy 1x run).
findings.fix: Split the context: export `useProgressActions()` from a second context that holds only the stable callbacks {answer, markClimax, reach, reset}. Use it in Ch10() (src/chapters/Ch10/index.tsx:121) and ChapterShell (src/components/Chapter.tsx), so they no longer re-render when the state changes. Components that read state (Hud, Quiz, Growth, LevelDesk) keep useProgress().

findings.problem: DOM size with every chapter mounted, which users reach by the epilogue because mounting is cumulative, is very large. It makes every whole-document style recalc, ScrollTrigger.refresh and forced layout expensive.
findings.evidence: ?mount=all: 32,195 elements, 25,913 of them inside 329 SVGs; outerHTML 6.4 MB; 1.94 MB of path `d` strings; max depth 23. Chapters: ch10 4,735, ch9 3,299, ch8 2,793, ch7 2,768, epilogue 2,726. Largest scenes: ch10-decision 1,034 (78 KB path data), ch10-serve 967, epilogue-cycle 895 (170 KB path data), ch8-solution 834, ch5-distributed 702.
